business_description: A fast-casual Mexican restaurant in Chicago's Logan Square neighborhood with annual revenue declining from $680K to $520K over three years; the owner handles all cash sales personally and reconciles them to a POS system on a weekly basis.
key_risk_narrative: Declining revenue, high Prime Cost (~68%), and a cash-heavy operation with owner-managed cash handling create both a repayment capacity risk and a documentation reliability risk that make normalized DSCR difficult to establish with confidence.
discrepancy_description: Bank statements show a recurring $2,200/month ACH outflow to an entity not identified in the tax return liabilities schedule, consistent with an undisclosed equipment financing obligation that would reduce adjusted DSCR below 1.00x.
